questions.question: You need to distinguish “Henderson–Hasselbalch equation” from several related chapter concepts. Which description uniquely identifies it?

options.label: A
options.text: The selective reduction of a nitrile to an aldehyde using diisobutylaluminum hydride followed by aqueous hydrolysis.

options.label: B
options.text: An organic compound containing a cyano functional group (-C≡N) where carbon is triply bonded to nitrogen.

options.label: C
options.text: The enhancement of carboxylic acid acidity caused by nearby electronegative substituents pulling electron density away from the carboxylate center.

options.label: D
options.text: A mathematical formula relating solution pH, acid pKa, and the ratio of conjugate base to acid concentrations: pH = pKa + log([A-]/[HA]).

questions.correct_answer: A mathematical formula relating solution pH, acid pKa, and the ratio of conjugate base to acid concentrations: pH = pKa + log([A-]/[HA]).
questions.explanation: The distinguishing description for Henderson–Hasselbalch equation is: A mathematical formula relating solution pH, acid pKa, and the ratio of conjugate base to acid concentrations: pH = pKa + log([A-]/[HA]).
